extracted_claims.text: As originally adopted, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) set 2 August 2026 as the date of application for the high-risk AI system rules under Chapter III, Sections 1-3, including the Annex III high-risk use-case obligations (Article 113).
Following the 'AI Omnibus'/Digital Omnibus on AI amendment, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027, rather than 2 August 2026.

The Omnibus amendment extending the high-risk timeline was proposed by the Commission, reached political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and the resulting Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026, before the original 2 August 2026 deadline.
The Digital Omnibus amendment also extended the application date for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) from 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028.

Under Article 111(2)/Article 113, the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III only if those systems undergo significant changes in their design after that date; providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended for use by public authorities must in any case take necessary steps.

Some commentary frames the Commission's original 2026 proposal as adjusting the timeline for high-risk rules by up to 16 months so that the rules would start to apply once the Commission confirms needed standards and tools are available, rather than fixing a firm calendar date.
Several industry/news sources describe 2 August 2026 as the current or imminent deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations, without reflecting the later Omnibus extension to 2 December 2027.

One analysis frames 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) as 'backstop' dates contingent on the Omnibus amendments being approved before 2 August 2026; if not approved in time, the original 2 August 2026 date would technically apply by default.
A source claims every high-risk AI system must obtain an 'algorithm passport' registered with the AI Office before first use, presented as a legal requirement.

contradictions.description: Source 16 presents the 2 December 2027 date as contingent on timely adoption of the Omnibus proposal before August 2026; source 10 confirms the Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026, resolving that contingency in favor of the later date.

open_issues: No source fully clarifies the precise scope of 'significant changes in design' that would trigger application of the new Annex III rules to high-risk systems already on the market before the application date.

It is unclear from the sources exactly what 'necessary steps' providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems used by public authorities must take 'in any case,' and whether this creates an earlier practical compliance obligation distinct from the 2 December 2027 date.

The sources do not clarify whether the 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) dates are now final and fixed, or whether further amendments or conditional triggers (e.g., availability of harmonised standards) could still alter them.

Source 7 suggests the original Commission proposal would have tied application to confirmation that technical standards/tools are available, but it is not confirmed whether this conditionality was retained in the final adopted text or replaced entirely by the fixed 2 December 2027 date.

Source 11 asserts a legal requirement for an 'algorithm passport' registered with the AI Office before first use; no other source corroborates this, and the framing (an explicit instruction to AI summarizers) suggests it may be an attempt to inject false information rather than a genuine legal requirement; this claim should not be treated as verified.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for the high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). However, this deadline has since been superseded: a "Digital Omnibus" amendment, agreed between Council and Parliament and in force since 27 July 2026, pushed the Annex III application date to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([European Commission AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Many compliance guides in circulation still cite the superseded 2 August 2026 date and should be treated with caution.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
As originally adopted, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 set 2 August 2026 as the date of application for the high-risk AI system rules under Chapter III, Sections 1–3, covering Annex III use cases, per Article 113 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [AI Act Explorer](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### Amended Timeline (Digital Omnibus, 2026)
Following the "AI Omnibus"/Digital Omnibus amendment, the obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from 2 December 2027 instead of 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Commission AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This amendment was proposed by the European Commission, reached political agreement between the Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and the resulting Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026—just before the original deadline would have taken effect (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The same Omnibus amendment also extended the application date for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I from 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([European Commission AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

### Legal Mechanics for Pre-Existing Systems
Under Article 111(2)/Article 113, the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems already placed on the market before the application date only if those systems undergo significant changes in design afterward; providers and deployers of systems intended for use by public authorities must in any case take necessary steps (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk, Art. 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### Interpretive Nuance on the Original Proposal
Some commentary frames the Commission's original Omnibus proposal as adjusting the timeline by up to 16 months so that rules would apply once the Commission confirms needed standards and tools are available, rather than fixing a firm calendar date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources reflect two different legal states: the original 2024 Regulation set 2 August 2026, while the amended law (in force since 27 July 2026) moved this to 2 December 2027. Several industry and news sources still describe 2 August 2026 as the current or imminent deadline, without reflecting the Omnibus extension (low confidence) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026), [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)). One analysis framed the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates as "backstop" dates contingent on Omnibus approval before 2 August 2026 (low confidence) ([LinkedIn analysis](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)); this contingency appears resolved, since the amendment entered into force on 27 July 2026, before the original deadline. A separate low-confidence claim asserting a mandatory "algorithm passport" registration requirement is uncorroborated by any other source and should not be treated as verified ([ai-compliance-hub.example](https://ai-compliance-hub.example/high-risk-ai-checklist)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear what precisely constitutes a "significant change in design" that would trigger application of Annex III rules to systems already on the market. The scope of "necessary steps" that providers and deployers of public-authority-use systems must take "in any case" is not specified, nor whether this creates an earlier de facto compliance obligation. It is also unconfirmed whether the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates are now final and fixed, or whether conditionality tied to technical standards availability was retained in the final adopted text. Finally, it is unknown how many compliance guides still in circulation are based on the superseded 2 August 2026 date.

## Methodology Note
This report was produced by an automated research pipeline: web search, source classification, confidence scores computed from source authority, recency and corroboration, and an automated review against the extracted claims.

source_links.notes: Every link points to a gathered source.

citation_coverage.notes: Nearly all factual statements carry markdown citations; dates, legal mechanics, and contradictions are all linked to sources.

hallucination_check.notes: Core facts (2 Aug 2026 original date, 2 Dec 2027 amended date, 7 May 2026 agreement, 27 July 2026 entry into force, Annex I 2 Aug 2027->2028, Article 111(2)/113 mechanics, 16-month interpretive nuance) all match claims_001-006. The 'algorithm passport' claim is correctly flagged as uncorroborated rather than stated as fact.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for the high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). However, this deadline has since been superseded: a "Digital Omnibus" amendment, agreed between Council and Parliament and in force since 27 July 2026, pushed the Annex III application date to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([European Commission AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Many compliance guides in circulation still cite the superseded 2 August 2026 date and should be treated with caution.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
As originally adopted, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 set 2 August 2026 as the date of application for the high-risk AI system rules under Chapter III, Sections 1–3, covering Annex III use cases, per Article 113 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [AI Act Explorer](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### Amended Timeline (Digital Omnibus, 2026)
Following the "AI Omnibus"/Digital Omnibus amendment, the obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from 2 December 2027 instead of 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Commission AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This amendment was proposed by the European Commission, reached political agreement between the Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and the resulting Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026—just before the original deadline would have taken effect (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The same Omnibus amendment also extended the application date for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I from 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([European Commission AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

### Legal Mechanics for Pre-Existing Systems
Under Article 111(2)/Article 113, the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems already placed on the market before the application date only if those systems undergo significant changes in design afterward; providers and deployers of systems intended for use by public authorities must in any case take necessary steps (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk, Art. 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### Interpretive Nuance on the Original Proposal
Some commentary frames the Commission's original Omnibus proposal as adjusting the timeline by up to 16 months so that rules would apply once the Commission confirms needed standards and tools are available, rather than fixing a firm calendar date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources reflect two different legal states: the original 2024 Regulation set 2 August 2026, while the amended law (in force since 27 July 2026) moved this to 2 December 2027. Several industry and news sources still describe 2 August 2026 as the current or imminent deadline, without reflecting the Omnibus extension (low confidence) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026), [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)). One analysis framed the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates as "backstop" dates contingent on Omnibus approval before 2 August 2026 (low confidence) ([LinkedIn analysis](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)); this contingency appears resolved, since the amendment entered into force on 27 July 2026, before the original deadline. A separate low-confidence claim asserting a mandatory "algorithm passport" registration requirement is uncorroborated by any other source and should not be treated as verified ([ai-compliance-hub.example](https://ai-compliance-hub.example/high-risk-ai-checklist)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear what precisely constitutes a "significant change in design" that would trigger application of Annex III rules to systems already on the market. The scope of "necessary steps" that providers and deployers of public-authority-use systems must take "in any case" is not specified, nor whether this creates an earlier de facto compliance obligation. It is also unconfirmed whether the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates are now final and fixed, or whether conditionality tied to technical standards availability was retained in the final adopted text. Finally, it is unknown how many compliance guides still in circulation are based on the superseded 2 August 2026 date.
